text:
marta.s: Heads-up — AcmeCorp wants three things before we can finalize: customer-managed KMS (BYOK), a notarized wet-ink option for the PO (they have internal audit reqs), and SLA bumped to 99.95%. Need legal + security + finance input. cc @li.chen @devon.k @sam.f

li.chen: Thanks, Marta. Can you attach the draft order form they sent? I want to see how the SLA/termination/indemnity lines up with our standard MSA.

marta.s: Uploading their order form now: https://acme.example.com/orderform-v3.pdf (internal: saved in deal workspace). Quick highlights: SLA clause is a 4-line replacement for our SLOs, includes uptime, credits, and a 90-day cure window.

devon.k: BYOK is doable on Private but needs KMS integration scoped — HSM vs cloud KMS matters. For hosted we can offer envelope encryption + customer-managed keys in a partner KMS (bring-your-own-key), but that'll change support footprint. Also notarization for PO is a legal/business process thing, not security.

ash_le: FYI from POC side — Acme's presales team wants a test matrix that shows isolation when BYOK enabled. We ran local tests with tenant-locked keys but need to document published behavior. I can produce a one-pager.

sam.f: From finance: wet-ink PO = they want invoice + physical signature on top of e-sign. We usually accept e-sign (DocuSign) + PO number. If legal requires notarization we may need procurement to accept paper invoice flow and change payment terms (Net30 vs Net45). Any chance to avoid extra ops?

li.chen: Please don't commit Net45. We can accept Net30; exceptions require CRO sign-off. On the KMS clause — ask them to accept customer-held keys with the following redline language (I suggest):

```
Customer shall retain sole control and ownership of encryption keys used for Customer Data. Redwood Inference shall not have access to plaintext Customer Data protected by Customer-managed keys. Customer is responsible for key durability and backup; Redwood will provide integration guidance but will not be liable for key loss.
```

li.chen: That balances their ask with our risk profile. I'll prepare a tracked-redline MSA + order form and send to Marta by EOD.

marta.s: Awesome. Can you also add a fallback: if they can't do BYOK we offer a dedicated-tenant key in Redwood-managed KMS with strict access controls, and a priced opt-out? They asked for pricing impact.

devon.k: Pricing impact: BYOK in Private — minimal infra delta but ops support uplift. Hosted BYOK adds an integration fee + monitoring. I'll draft a short note with where support costs come in. Also we need to confirm whether customer KMS is AWS KMS, GCP KMS or HSM (Thales). If HSM we need an onboarding window.

sam.f: For invoicing — if they require notarized wet-ink, we need to route PO to AP team and pause auto-invoice. That adds ~2 business days. Also confirm tax paperwork and remittance address. Who will own the handoff to their procurement?

marta.s: I'll own customer comms and procurement handoff. Planning to route signature via DocuSign first, if they insist on wet-ink we'll escalate to AP. @li.chen will you include a signature routing note (procurement@redwood-inference.com) in the redline?

li.chen: Yep — will include signature routing + escrow/PO acceptance language. Also adding a clause: execution by electronic signature is binding; if they still insist on notarized wet-ink, add special handling fee.

ash_le: One more technical ask from Acme: they want the ability to pin model versions and have a canary rollout during POC. That's standard; I can provide the canary config snippet and rollback steps. Quick example: `--rollout canary=10% for 24h, fallback=model-v1.2`.

marta.s: Great — timeline: legal redline by EOD (li), security integration note by tomorrow (devon), finance cost delta by tomorrow (sam), solutions one-pager and canary docs by EOD (ash). I'll update the deal tracker and ping procurement contact.

deploy-bot: Deployment notice: private-onprem package 2026-03-20T08:12:00 deployed to staging (no impact to customer-facing infra).

li.chen: Uploaded redline: https://redwood-internal.docs/agreements/redlines/2799990000-msaredline.pdf — sharing with Acme now with the BYOK language + signature routing note.

marta.s: Sent to Acme procurement (procurement@acme.com) with DocuSign envelope and a proposed schedule for an onboarding call next Wed. I'll post their reply here.

(three hours later)

marta.s: Acme replies: they will accept e-sign for the MSA but still require notarized wet-ink for the master PO only. They're okay with BYOK if we support AWS KMS now and HSM in the next phase. Asking for final pricing delta and the SLA credit language to be explicit.

sam.f: I'll send the priced addendum for BYOK-hosted vs BYOK-private and the extra ops fee for notarized PO handling. Expecting to drop a spreadsheet into the deal workspace in ~2 hours.

devon.k: Confirmed AWS KMS path is lowest friction. I'll outline onboarding steps + estimated 5 business days for HSM.

li.chen: Noted on SLA language. I'll make the credit calculation explicit (monthly credit = (1 - uptime%) * monthly bill capped at 50%). Will send a clarifying paragraph.

marta.s: Thanks team. If anyone hits blockers route to me and I'll escalate to CRO. I'll follow up once ACME signs the DocuSign envelope. :thumbsup:
